Its panel is genuinely complex, but too few charts came back to show whether the high codes are supported.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The panel does skew complex, and only a small share of 99215s fall on 0–1 condition patients. But the by-complexity table shows this provider's 99215 share running several times the all-provider share within every tier, including 0-condition visits. A sicker panel alone would not produce that, and it is why the risk-adjusted score stays high. The low-complexity sample includes 99215s on single routine diagnoses, such as C0103348 (abdominal pain, no chronic conditions) and C0103880 (Z09 follow-up only), which deserve chart review. The documentation that exists leans the other way: all four documented 99215s, including C0104160, were supported at high MDM. Only one 99214 (C0103599) was documented below billed. The cloned-note signal is negligible. With records on under 2% of claims and only four documented 99215s, the documentation is too thin to confirm or rule out upcoding. A reviewer should first request charts for the 0–2 condition 99215 claims, starting with the sampled low-complexity examples, to see whether the elevation in those tiers holds up on review."}
